# Iris

> Iris is a live-wallpaper engine for Linux and Windows. `iris-daemon` presents stills, Wallpaper Engine packages, scenes, Linux video, and HTML behind the desktop. A Tauri manager applies wallpapers over length-prefixed JSON-RPC and does not render. Version 0.1.0, protocol version 1, Apache License 2.0.

Facts an agent needs before editing or answering:

- Linux presents on a Wayland layer-shell surface and paces frames with `wl_surface.frame`. Windows presents a borderless window reparented onto the desktop WorkerW. macOS has no backend.
- The manager (`src-tauri`, React) must not link Wayland, wgpu, or FFmpeg. Those stay in the daemon crates.
- IPC is JSON-RPC 2.0 with a little-endian `u32` length prefix. Frames above 16 MiB are rejected. Linux uses `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/iris/iris.sock` or `/tmp/iris-$UID.sock`. Windows uses `\\.\pipe\iris-ipc-{user}`.
- Video decode is Linux-only (VA-API, then NVDEC, then software). Web wallpapers load `iris://wallpaper/index.html` through wry. Paths that contain `..` or leave the wallpaper root are rejected.
- Scene uniforms are a packed 344-byte prefix. The full frame uniform, including telemetry, is 552 bytes. Do not insert `vec3` padding.
- Workspace `rust-version` is 1.80. A full build needs Rust 1.85 or newer because wry 0.57 requires it. Run one Cargo command at a time. `cargo fmt` must not be given `--edition`.
- `cargo test --offline --lib` does not launch a webview or a compositor. `cargo test --workspace` also builds the Tauri shell.

- [README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ayoubzulfiqar/iris/main/README.md): What Iris is, how to run the daemon and the manager, and the verification commands
- [Architecture](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ayoubzulfiqar/iris/main/docs/architecture.md): Process split, crate map, frame clocks, uniform layout, and failure isolation
- [IPC](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ayoubzulfiqar/iris/main/docs/ipc.md): Frame format, methods, wallpaper config, and compatibility rules
